title: SLO-slope adaptive admission + stochastic connection thinning for cross-region stores
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional surges we observe cascading tail-latency increases when Redis/Kafka/primary DB endpoints slow down. Existing hard circuit breakers and naive global connection throttles either (a) cut too abruptly causing capacity loss for high-priority tenants, or (b) allow slow degradation that violates SLOs.

Goal: Implement an SLO-driven admission controller that uses a "slope" model (SLO headroom over time) to decide admission and a stochastic connection thinning mechanism to probabilistically shed lower-priority sessions while preserving burst capacity for critical lanes. This ticket covers design, core runtime implementation (agent + server-side policy), a canary rollout to two regions, and instrumentation to verify SLO compliance and fairness across tenants.

Key outcomes: predictable SLO preservation, preserved tail latency for P0 tenants, graceful degradation of background/low-priority workloads, and clear observability for operators to tune thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes an admission API that computes per-request allow/deny with reason codes (SLO_SLOPE, THINNED_STOCHASTIC, CIRCUIT_OPEN)
Connection thinning implemented as per-policy probability function (p = f(headroom, pool_util, tenant_priority)) and exercised in load tests
Canary in us-west1 and eu-central1 demonstrates <1% P0 SLO violations under synthetic 2x regional surge vs baseline (before changes) and background throughput reduced by >=65% for P3 lanes
Dashboard panels added: per-region SLO headroom slope, thinning probability heatmap, per-tenant allowed vs dropped requests, circuit state transitions
Graceful fallback: when Redis/Kafka primary becomes unavailable, system routes reads to read-replica with annotation and keeps writes queued to local buffer for 300s as defined in playbook
Automated chaos tests cover transient 500ms latency shifts and 10s outages for downstreams and assert no cascading failures in control plane
implementation_plan: 2) New admission library (go/rwdn/admission) with programmable policies and pluggable metrics backend - 5 days
3) Integrate into connection-manager: per-tenant token accounting and stochastic thinning hook - 3 days
4) Circuit-breaker harmonization: map existing breaker states to admission reasons and add hysteresis window - 2 days
5) E2E staging tests + infra for canary rollout (feature flag) - 3 days
6) Observability: Prometheus metrics + Grafana dashboards + alert rules - 2 days
7) Run multi-region load tests and capture replay traces for postmortem - 2 days
notes: Design tradeoffs considered: deterministic token-bucket admission vs probabilistic thinning. Deterministic offers stronger SLAs per-tenant but leads to brittle behavior under bursty arrival patterns. We chose a hybrid: token bank for P0/P1, stochastic thinning for P2/P3 to reclaim headroom smoothly.
We will keep per-tenant minimum reservation windows (min_guarantee_ms) so short spikes from tenant frontends are not immediately cut off.
To limit blast radius, initial rollout gated by feature flag and limited to 5% traffic in each region during canary. Rollout plan in rollout_plan.
Open question: should eviction of KV cache entries be accelerated for thinned requests to reduce memory pressure? Decision deferred to follow-up ticket after canary metrics.

We benchmarked several probability curves in local sim harness; a logistic curve parameterized by headroom and pool_util provided best tradeoff between served P0 requests and background drop rate. Config defaults included in runtime-1.23.
Coordination: Need product buy-in for explicit behavior when local read-replica returns stale results (consistency doc linked).
rollout_plan: Phase A (Dev/staging): unit + integration tests. Validate admission decisions are idempotent and reason codes propagate to logs - done
Phase B (Canary 5%): enable in us-west1 and eu-central1 behind ff:admission-slope-stochastic - 3 days observing metrics
Phase C (Canary 25%): expand to 25% in those regions if no regression in SLOs and error rates
Phase D (Regional ramp): progressive increase per-region with automatic rollback trigger on >0.5% increase in P0 SLO violations over 15m window
Phase E (Global): enable for all regions and add tuning knobs per-regional traffic profile
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission math and probability function boundary cases
Integration tests that simulate a cross-region store latency increase and verify admission state transitions and circuit persistence
Load testing with k6 + chaos harness to inject 500ms latencies and 5s outages for Redis and Kafka
A/B canary analysis scripts: compare baseline vs canary traces and compute PASSED/FAILED for SLO budgets
Customer scenario tests: heavy embedding workloads + normal chat traffic to verify fairness
